note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Solomon Islands: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: The first SBD 30,080 of an individual's income is tax-free; above it the next $15,000 is taxed at 11%, the next $15,000 at 23%, the next $30,000 at 35% and the rest at 40%.
figures.applies: Individuals, employees and self-employed, from January 2020

sources.said: From January 2020, the personal tax exemption threshold for individuals was increased from $15,080 to $30,080. This means that individuals – both employees and self‑employed persons are not required to pay tax on the first $30,080 of their income. For any income earnt over $30,080.00 the rates of tax remain the same as set out below: Income Bracket Rate $1 to $15 000 11% $15 001 to $30 000 $1,650 + 23% of excess $30 001 to $60 000 $5,100 + 35% of excess $60 001 and over $15,600 + 40% of excess

figures.finding: To the National Provident Fund the employee pays at least 5% and the employer 7.5% of gross wages, once an employee has worked six or more days and earned $20 or more in a month.
figures.applies: Employees, including under a contract for service

sources.said: Under the SINPF Act, members contribute a minimum of 5% of their wages and employers contribute 7.5% on behalf of each employee. Together this makes a total monthly contribution of 12.5%, which is credited to the employee's individual member account. … An employer is any person, company, association or body of persons employing an employee under a contract of service, apprenticeship or a contract for service. An employer becomes liable to pay monthly contributions once an employee has worked six or more days and been paid a wage of $20.00 or more in a month.

figures.finding: Employers deduct PAYE at each payment using IRD tables and pay it by the 15th of the next month.

sources.said: Inland Revenue provides tables that tell you how much to deduct depending on whether you pay weekly, fortnightly, bi-monthly or monthly. … All PAYE taxes deducted during the month must be paid to IRD by the 15th day of the following month.

figures.finding: Payments to non-residents for professional services bear 20% withholding, royalties 15% and film-hire rent 5%; the tax deducted under section 38 is a final tax when correctly deducted and paid; "professional services" means professional or technical services or those of an adviser or consultant, and the Act names no separate rule for performers.
figures.applies: Payments made to non-residents; whether a performer's fee is "professional services" is not stated in the Act (the game reads it so).

sources.said: Payments Made to Non-Residents Interest 15% Professional Services 20% Royalties 15% Contracting (installation, maintenance, construction, erection, clearing and draining) 7.5% Income from ships and aircraft 5% Insurance Premiums and premiums on insurance 15% Rent for Hiring of Films 5%

A person who pays non-resident income to a non-resident person shall deduct therefrom tax at the appropriate withholding rate specified in the Sixth Schedule in force at the date on which such income is payable
(e) section 38. … (3) If this section applies, the tax deducted shall be a final tax on the income of the recipient in respect of which the tax has been deducted

“professional services” means any payment for professional or technical services or services of an adviser or consultant on behalf of a person or entity resident in Solomon Islands (whether such services are rendered wholly or partly in Solomon Islands or outside Solomon Islands)

figures.finding: Royalties paid to a resident bear 10% withholding.

sources.said: Payments Made to Residents Contracting (installation, maintenance, construction, erection, clearing and draining) 7.5% Royalties 10%

figures.finding: There is no VAT; sales tax of 10% is charged on listed services, including professional services, and returned monthly by the 30th; the Act sets no turnover threshold: every person who sells prescribed services must apply to register.

sources.said: Services provided by hairdressers, barbers & beauty shops 10% Casino entrance fee $5 Laundry services 10% Tyre services 10% Professional Services 10%

every person who in Solomon Islands sells prescribed goods or services shall apply to the Commissioner in the prescribed form for registration as a seller of prescribed goods and services together with the prescribed fee.

figures.finding: The income year generally ends on 31 December and the return is due by 31 March after it.

sources.said: Returns are due by 31 March following the year of income unless you have approval for an extension of time or operate on a different balance date. … For most businesses, the accounting year ends on 31 December but it may be a different month – this is the balance date.
